questions.question: display: grid does what?
options: Turns children into flex items on one axis.
Makes the element a grid container; children become grid items.
questions.explanation: An element with display: grid becomes a grid container. Its child elements then become grid items.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: An element with display: grid becomes a grid container. Its child elements then become grid items.

questions.question: Grid layout is?
questions.explanation: The CSS grid lets you define a two-dimensional layout of columns and rows and then place elements within the grid.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: The CSS grid lets you define a two-dimensional layout of columns and rows and then place elements within the grid.

questions.question: Flexbox vs grid, Grant's framing?
options: Grid replaced flexbox; never use both.
Flexbox is a big brother to nothing; grid is the two-dimensional companion.
questions.explanation: Flexbox has a big brother: Grid Layout. Together they provide a full-featured layout engine.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: It has a big brother: another new specification called the Grid Layout Module.

questions.question: What does 1fr 1fr 1fr declare?
options: Three columns of equal leftover space.
questions.explanation: grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr defines three columns of equal width.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: As with flexbox, grid applies to how many DOM levels?
options: Two: the container and its children.
questions.explanation: As with flexbox, grid layout applies to two levels of the DOM hierarchy.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: As with flexbox, grid layout applies to two levels of the DOM hierarchy.

questions.question: Can an item span multiple columns?
options: Yes. Some elements fill one cell; others span columns or rows.
questions.explanation: Some elements may only fill one cell of the grid; others can span multiple columns or rows.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: Some elements may only fill one cell of the grid; others can span multiple columns or rows.

questions.question: Must you place every item by hand?
options: No. You can place items precisely or allow them to flow into the gaps.
questions.explanation: You can place items precisely within the grid, or allow them to flow naturally to fill in the gaps.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: You can place items precisely within the grid, or allow them to flow naturally to fill in the gaps.

questions.question: Which property sets the column tracks?
questions.explanation: Grant's basic grid listing uses grid-template-columns and grid-template-rows.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: grid-template-rows: 1fr 1fr means?
options: Two rows sharing leftover height equally.
questions.explanation: The listing defines two rows with 1fr 1fr after three columns.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: grid-column: 1 / 3 typically means?
options: Start at line 1, end at line 3 (span two tracks).
questions.explanation: Grid lines number the boundaries. 1 / 3 spans the first two columns.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: others can span multiple columns or rows.

questions.question: Why keep flexbox after learning grid?
options: Use them together for a cohesive page: grid for the page, flex for a row inside a cell.
questions.explanation: The chapter covers using flexbox and grid together to build a cohesive web page layout.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: Using flexbox and grid together to build a cohesive web page layout

questions.question: Which is a three-column grid?
questions.explanation: display: grid plus three 1fr tracks. There is no grid-flex value.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant

questions.question: Can the grid size itself to its contents?
options: Yes. Size can be precise, or the grid can size itself to fit the contents.
questions.explanation: The size of the grid can be defined precisely, or you can allow it to automatically size itself as needed to fit the contents within.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: The size of the grid can be defined precisely, or you can allow it to automatically size itself as needed to fit the contents within.

questions.question: What is wrong with .hero { display: grid-item; }?
options: grid-item is the correct display value.
Items become grid items because their parent is display: grid, not because of a display: grid-item value.
hero cannot be a grid child.
questions.explanation: Children of a grid container become grid items. There is no display: grid-item.

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
reference.excerpt: Its child elements then become grid items.

questions.question: minmax() is for?
options: A track that can grow between a minimum and a maximum.
questions.explanation: Grant's grid chapter includes minmax among the track sizing tools (PDF p. 193 in this file).

reference.book: CSS in Depth, 1st Edition by Keith J. Grant
